steps.what: Observe pictures through broadcast monitors and direct camera and video staff on shading and composition

tasks.design: Keep visual monitoring and direction human through {OTHER}, the broadcast picture monitoring and crew communication equipment. The technical director responds to actual pictures and the production's visual intent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shading and composition depend on changing visual content and creative context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native broadcast monitors and communication equipment already support the task.
tasks.still_hard: A technically measurable picture can still be compositionally wrong for the scene.
tasks.human_edge: The technical director recognises a useful visual adjustment and communicates it clearly to the crew.
tasks.altitude: Visual direction time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Adjust framing and exposure to production direction
reach.learn: Composition, shading and practical camera constraints

evidence.claim: Picture direction combines visual judgement and live crew communication; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is observing pictures and directing camera and video staff, excluding operating cameras, adjusting shading controls and subsequent editing. Crew execution remains unchanged outside the focal denominator.

Camera staff produce live pictures during normal production. Technical director observes them and gives directions within the full retained time; crew responses follow the relevant directions during the same live interaction, not as a prerequisite for the first observation.
No free structured composition or shading-quality flag is assumed. Keep existing native equipment; no new system or process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Whether direction occurs live or during recorded production
How creative and technical picture authority is divided
research_questions: Do camera and video staff understand and execute the director's picture instructions consistently?

already_counted.description: Observe pictures, judge shading and composition and communicate crew direction

incremental.description: No new system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Visual judgement and live direction keep full time; no crew or equipment runtime is counted as a focal saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign and supervise technical production duties

steps.what: Assign duties to workers producing and technically controlling radio and television programs
Supervise workers carrying out technical control and production duties and resolve difficulties

tasks.design: Keep duty assignment and technical supervision human, with current {PROJECT} records as a reference. The director evaluates staff capability and changing production conditions before allocating or revising duties.
tasks.previous_blocker: Allocating duties and supervising technical practice require knowledge of people and the live production.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native project records and communication arrangements already support the task.
tasks.still_hard: Availability alone does not establish that a worker can handle a particular technical responsibility.
tasks.human_edge: The director recognises practical limits and intervenes when the crew needs help.
tasks.altitude: Supervision time and authority over technical duties remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Technical duty allocation and supervision depend on contextual human judgement; no saving is inferred from scheduling capability.

assumptions: Boundary is the director's assignment and supervision, excluding roster administration, worker execution, individual technical training and creative direction. Shared supervision must have one owner.
Production managers and crew supply existing requirements, capability information and availability; director checks these during s1's 35 hours. No free structured competency or ready flag is assumed.

Workers produce their work and concerns after assignment, before the corresponding s2 observation. Director elicits, checks and records guidance within s2's 65 hours. Worker execution remains outside the focal denominator and is not reduced.
Keep native records and current supervision practice. No new tracking or allocation system means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which duties require specific qualifications or delegated authority
How staffing changes are currently communicated
research_questions: Can each worker state their technical responsibility and escalation route before production?

already_counted.description: Assess staff constraints, assign duties and supervise actual technical work

incremental.description: No changed process or new upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Assignment judgement and supervision retain full time; no worker execution time is included in the director's savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor broadcasts and assess whether programs conform to station or network policies and regulations

tasks.design: Keep substantive broadcast review human, using {OTHER}, the broadcast monitoring system, and current guidance in {DOCS}. The director observes content and technical presentation, records concerns and escalates uncertainty through the current management route.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy conformance can depend on the meaning and context of what is broadcast.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native monitoring and policy records support review; no automatic conformance classifier is required.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous content and changing guidance may need editorial or specialist interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The director identifies a meaningful issue beyond a formal timing or metadata check.
tasks.altitude: Broadcast review time and escalation responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Interpret programming guidelines in editorial context

evidence.claim: Substantive broadcast policy review requires contextual human assessment; fixed scheduling checks do not establish overall conformance.

assumptions: Boundary is substantive review of actual broadcasts, excluding native transmission monitoring runtime, schedule arithmetic, completed-log checks and specialist legal interpretation. Overlapping review actions must be allocated once across roles.

Broadcast teams produce the programme through their existing production work. Station or network policy owners and compliance specialists provide current guidance through existing work. Director reads, checks applicability and records observations within the retained 100 hours; no free structured compliant flag is assumed.
Applicable national requirements and escalation authority require customer confirmation. No particular legal rule or automatic legal conclusion is introduced.
Keep native monitoring and document records. No new classifier, recording or workflow means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which policies the technical director is responsible for reviewing
What specialist guidance applies to ambiguous programmes
research_questions: Can concerns be traced to the actual broadcast segment and the applicable guidance version?

already_counted.description: Observe broadcasts, assess context and record issues for escalation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Substantive viewing and policy interpretation keep full time; no timing-check or system-runtime saving is counted here.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train crew in broadcast equipment use

steps.what: Demonstrate operation of broadcast switchers, cameras, monitors, microphones and lights
Observe workers using equipment and coach correct technique during practice

tasks.design: Keep equipment demonstration and coached practice human on {OTHER}, the broadcast production equipment. Existing instructions in {DOCS} remain reference material while the director observes what workers can actually do.
tasks.previous_blocker: Knowing instructions does not establish practical equipment competence.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native manuals and actual equipment already support demonstration and practice.
tasks.still_hard: Workers need different explanations and may make mistakes that require immediate intervention.
tasks.human_edge: The director sees practical misunderstandings and adapts coaching to the worker and equipment.
tasks.altitude: Technical instruction and responsibility for observing practice remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Operational constraints and effective technical coaching

evidence.claim: Equipment training requires demonstration and observation of practice; no labour saving is claimed for replacing those interactions.

assumptions: Boundary is the director's technical training, excluding booking courses, maintaining manuals, certifying formal qualifications and workers' independent practice. Learner time is outside the focal denominator.
Equipment owners supply current instructions through existing support work. Director verifies suitability and demonstrates within s1's 45 hours; no new free structured teaching script is assumed.

Workers produce the observed equipment practice after demonstration, before its corresponding s2 feedback. Director observes, interprets and captures learning needs within s2's 55 hours; no automated competency flag is introduced.
Keep existing native resources and equipment. No new training tool or recording means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which equipment and worker experience levels are involved
What local supervision or qualification requirements apply
research_questions: Can workers demonstrate the required technique and identify when to seek assistance after coaching?

already_counted.description: Demonstrate equipment use, observe practice and coach workers

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Demonstration and coached practice retain full time; no learner effort or equipment runtime is counted as focal saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Visual direction, technical staff supervision, substantive broadcast review and hands-on equipment training remain human work with unchanged time.
reach: Work with camera operators on visual direction
Work with broadcast technicians on practical constraints and coaching
Work with programming directors on contextual policy review
skills_to_grow: Delegate technical duties against actual capability
role.ambitious_version: Provide clear technical leadership and evidence-based oversight while retaining responsibility for people, pictures and practical competence.
